findings.description: active_skus is a list, so each `scan.sku not in active_skus` is a linear scan over every active SKU. For each scan this costs O(number of active SKUs), so reconcile() is O(scans x active SKUs) overall. With a catalog of tens of thousands of SKUs and a similarly large stocktake, this becomes tens of billions of comparisons and reconcile() will take minutes or hours where it previously ran in linear time. The new unknown_locations pass is what introduces this cost.
findings.suggestion: Build a set once: active_skus = {item.sku for item in catalog.active()}. Membership tests then become O(1) and the function is linear in the number of scans and SKUs.
findings.title: Membership test against a list makes unknown-SKU detection quadratic
